activation_rule: pull requests created strictly after registration PR merge

motivation.prior_result: pr-review-validation/v1 failed the frozen absolute mean lead-time gate
motivation.v2_question: Can richer observable item-flow evidence support a frozen model that predicts the tail as well as the center on a genuinely future holdout?

cohort.selection: first eligible merged pull requests in creation-time order

candidate_tail_mechanisms.evidence_class: observed item delay; not human service time

candidate_tail_mechanisms.evidence: timestamp/calendar pattern only unless independent calendar evidence is supplied
residual elapsed delay after explicitly observed intervals
future source enrichment may include declared PR size proxies if frozen before Stage 2
candidate_tail_mechanisms.evidence_class: observed only if source rule is frozen before holdout

candidate_tail_mechanisms.evidence: not identified by public GitHub timestamp gaps

stage_rules.stage_1: collect exactly 18 eligible merged PRs and use them only for evidence scouting, calibration and model design
stage_rules.model_freeze_checkpoint: after Stage 1 is complete and before the first Stage 2 PR is eligible
stage_rules.stage_2: collect the next 12 eligible merged PRs as untouched holdout

model_freeze_requirements.mechanism_without_source_evidence: remain assumed/swept or stay out of v2

minimum_tail_reporting.reason: v1 matched the center substantially better than the observed upper-tail elapsed time

limits: Public GitHub events do not reconstruct conserved actor-time.
Review response latency is not reviewer service effort.
Residual elapsed time does not identify its causal mechanism.
Calendar effects remain inferable unless independent availability evidence exists.
The v2 result will apply to this repository/cohort/model class, not organizations generally.
